relations.definition: The biconcave disc geometry of an erythrocyte yields a higher surface-area-to-volume ratio than a sphere of similar diameter, increasing the area available for gas exchange.

support.quote: The biconcave shape also provides a greater surface area across which gas exchange can occur, relative to its volume; a sphere of a similar diameter would have a lower surface area-to-volume ratio.
This shape optimizes the ratio of surface area to volume, facilitating gas exchange.

relations.definition: Each heme iron ion in hemoglobin binds one oxygen molecule, so one hemoglobin molecule can transport four oxygen molecules, forming oxyhemoglobin in the lungs.

support.quote: Each iron ion in the heme can bind to one oxygen molecule; therefore, each hemoglobin molecule can transport four oxygen molecules.
In the lungs, hemoglobin picks up oxygen, which binds to the iron ions, forming oxyhemoglobin .

relations.definition: Flexible spectrin cytoskeletal proteins allow the erythrocyte to fold and spring back, enabling passage through narrow capillaries.

support.quote: their structural proteins like spectrin are flexible, allowing them to bend over themselves to a surprising degree, then spring back again when they enter a wider vessel.
This includes the protein spectrin, a cytoskeletal protein element.

relations.definition: Narrow capillary lumens force erythrocytes to fold as they pass, while slowing flow and extending the opportunity for gas exchange.

support.quote: Capillary beds are extremely narrow, slowing the passage of the erythrocytes and providing an extended opportunity for gas exchange to occur.
the space within capillaries can be so minute that, despite their own small size, erythrocytes may have to fold in on themselves if they are to make their way through.
